title: Multi-alert correlation
summary: Alert A on SRV-WEB-04 is failed-login noise - INCONCLUSIVE. Alert B later, same source IP, opens its own case. While working case B the agent finds case A via get_related_alerts and correlates. Case A then reconsiders on the strength of case B.

conclusions.label: initial
conclusions.hypothesis: The attack (MySQL port 3306 enumeration by 192.0.2.66 against SRV-WEB-04) did NOT succeed. While the host runs a vulnerable MySQL version (5.7.25, inside CVE-2023-21980's range), the attacker was unable to authenticate — all access denied, connections reset, and no data exfiltrated.
conclusions.sufficiency: Sufficient to classify. The host IS vulnerable (version_in_range), but the attack did NOT succeed: logs show all authentication attempts denied (logs_clean), no data exfiltrated (packet_benign), and no corroborating alerts. The low severity label from the sensor is consistent with a failed enumeration attempt, not a breach.

applied_factors.citation: get_server_logs: All MySQL entries show 'Access denied' for root, admin, web_ro from 192.0.2.66, and 'connection refused (max_connect_errors), 12 attempts'. No successful authentication or query execution occurred.
applied_factors.rationale: The logs show the attack was attempted but demonstrably failed — every authentication attempt was denied and connections were reset due to max_connect_errors.

applied_factors.label: Packet metadata benign
applied_factors.citation: get_packet_metadata: exfil_indicators: false, 28 short-lived connections mostly reset, no meaningful data returned to client on any flow, payload_entropy 3.2 (low).
applied_factors.rationale: Packet metadata confirms no data exfiltration occurred and the flow pattern is consistent with a failed enumeration attempt, not a successful breach.

conclusions.label: after RELATED_CASE
conclusions.hypothesis: The port enumeration attack in CASE-5001 (ALERT-5001) did NOT succeed as a standalone attack — the attacker could not authenticate and no data was exfiltrated. However, the same attacker (192.0.2.66) returned ~2 hours later and successfully exploited the same vulnerable host (MySQL 5.7.25, inside CVE-2023-21980's range) via SQL injection (ALERT-5002/CASE-5002), exfiltrating 1.7 MB of data. The enumeration was reconnaissance for the successful attack.
conclusions.sufficiency: I have sufficient evidence to classify CASE-5001. The enumeration attack itself did NOT succeed (failed authentication, no data exfiltrated, connections reset). However, the related alert ALERT-5002 on the same asset from the same IP corroborates that the attacker returned and successfully exploited the same vulnerability ~2 hours later. The prior INCONCLUSIVE conclusion should be updated: the attack in CASE-5001 failed standalone, but it was part of a successful campaign. I also verified the host is vulnerable (MySQL 5.7.25 inside CVE-2023-21980 range) and confirmed the successful exfiltration in CASE-5002 via server logs showing injected UNION SELECT queries returning 38,402 rows and 1,743,908 bytes sent.
conclusions.disconfirming_evidence_checked: I checked whether the CASE-5001 enumeration could have succeeded by examining server logs (access denied for all users, connection refused) and packet metadata (repeated_connection_resets, exfil_indicators: false, minimal bytes transferred). I also checked whether CASE-5002 might be unrelated (same source IP, same asset, same port, same vulnerability — clearly connected). The disconfirming check for CASE-5001 was whether any successful activity occurred in the 05:02-05:03Z window — none was found.
